cues: Excess mercury gives the mercurous salt, mercury one, which is really a pair of mercury atoms bonded together.
Excess acid or halogen gives the mercuric salt, mercury two.
So limited chlorine gives calomel, excess chlorine gives mercuric chloride.
Cold dilute nitric acid with excess mercury gives mercurous nitrate, hot concentrated acid gives mercuric nitrate.
Dilute hydrochloric and sulphuric acids do nothing.
text: Mercury follows one rule. Excess mercury gives the mercurous salt, mercury one, which is really a pair of mercury atoms bonded together. Excess acid or halogen gives the mercuric salt, mercury two. So limited chlorine gives calomel, excess chlorine gives mercuric chloride. Cold dilute nitric acid with excess mercury gives mercurous nitrate, hot concentrated acid gives mercuric nitrate. Dilute hydrochloric and sulphuric acids do nothing.
